standard_prerequisites.name: Base change behaviour of the relative assassin, and vanishing of a module with no weakly associated points
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, labels divisors-lemma-base-change-relative-assassin (proof line 6615), divisors-remark-base-change-relative-assassin (proof line 6616), divisors-lemma-weakly-ass-zero (proof line 6623) and divisors-lemma-ses-weakly-ass (proof line 6626)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first two show that the hypothesis that the relative associated points lie in the image is stable under base change; the third reduces injectivity to the vanishing of the weakly associated points of the kernel, and the fourth places those inside the weakly associated points of the module itself.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weakly associated points of a flat finite type module lie in the relative assassin
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-bourbaki-finite-type-general-base, invoked at proof line 6628 and claimed separately as S14-algebra-bourbaki-general-base
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that for a flat finite type module every weakly associated point is a relative associated point, so the hypothesis controls all the weakly associated points of the kernel.

standard_prerequisites.name: Faithful flatness of a flat local ring map and its consequence of universal injectivity
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective, invoked at proof line 6641
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the map obtained by tensoring the stalk of the module with the local ring upstairs injective, which is what forces the stalk of the kernel to vanish at every relevant point.

core_obligations: Reduce to the injectivity statement over S: the final assertion that injectivity survives any base change follows because both the hypothesis on the relative associated points and the flatness and finite type assumptions are preserved by base change, so it suffices to prove that the displayed arrow is injective (proof lines 6611-6618).

Reduce injectivity to a statement about the kernel: let K be the kernel of the canonical map, and note that it suffices to prove that the weakly associated points of K are empty, since a module with no weakly associated points vanishes; the weakly associated points of the kernel are contained in those of the module (proof lines 6619-6626).

Conclude pointwise: because the module is flat and of finite type, its weakly associated points are relative associated points, and by hypothesis each of those is the image of a point of X'; flatness of the morphism makes the corresponding local ring map faithfully flat, so tensoring the stalk with the upstairs local ring is injective, which says precisely that the stalk of the kernel vanishes; hence the kernel is zero and the canonical map is injective and remains so after base change (proof lines 6627-6642).
proof_roadmap: Base change stability reduces the statement to injectivity over the base (proof lines 6611-6618).
Replace injectivity by the vanishing of the weakly associated points of the kernel (proof lines 6619-6626).
Use flatness, the weak Bourbaki lemma and faithful flatness of the local rings to kill the kernel pointwise (proof lines 6627-6642).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for the canonical map from a flat finite type module to the pushforward of its pullback along a flat morphism to be injective, namely that the relative associated points of the module lie in the image of the morphism, and shows this property is stable under base change (statement lines 6597-6609, tag 05PD). The proof reduces base change stability to the same statement over the base, replaces injectivity by the vanishing of the weakly associated points of the kernel, uses that for a flat finite type module those points are relative associated ones, and then kills the kernel at each such point by faithful flatness of the induced local ring map. The chain of reductions through weakly associated points is the substance, so the claim is H2.
